biography.plain_text: Sam Gershowitz is an American recycling entrepreneur, founder and owner of Long Island-based Gershow Recycling. He began the company in 1964 with $1,000 borrowed from his parents, a rented Central Islip yard and his brother Lou as partner. Processing discarded vehicles grew into a large regional metal-recycling business whose operations remain under family leadership.

long_biography.plain_text:
Long Island's discarded cars supplied Sam Gershowitz with the idea that became Gershow Recycling. While driving to the Hamptons, he noticed vehicles and appliances abandoned along roads and later found municipal landfills filled with car hulks. He paid towns a dollar per car, recovered thousands and sold the crushed metal to local scrap dealers.

The young company built its own portable car flattener and improvised with used equipment. During a severe recession, Gershowitz bought his brother out and committed to an expensive shredder that he assembled with mechanic Joe Bertuccio. He also renamed the business as environmental awareness spread. The Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries recognised his decades of work with its Lifetime Achievement Award.
